chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darradj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the prayer on a ship. He said, 'Indeed, a man came to my father (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq) and asked him, saying: I am on a ship and the sea is rough/close to me, so I go out and pray upon it. He (Abu Ja'far) said to him: Do you not accept that you pray with the prayer of Noah (peace be upon him)?'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for praying on a ship when the sea is rough according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) responds to a traveler's query about praying on a ship during rough seas by referencing the prayer of Prophet Noah (AS). This allusion highlights the flexibility of *Qasr* (shortening) and *Jam'* (combining) prayers during travel, emphasizing that the believer should accept the ease granted by Allah in such conditions, mirroring the prophetic precedent. The narration underscores the practical application of divine leniency (*rukhas*) in Shia jurisprudence for those facing physical difficulty while traveling.
